item.title: Local efforts promote aging-friendly communities and social connection
item.description: Community groups are joining statewide efforts to boost the quality of life for Wisconsin’s growing population of seniors, as projections show the number of people aged 65 and older could top 1.5 million by 2040. The post Local efforts promote aging-friendly communities and social connection appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Other states have legalized weed. Why hasn’t Wisconsin?
item.description: Wisconsin lawmakers have introduced bills for the past 13 years to legalize marijuana. They never pass. But why? The post Other states have legalized weed. Why hasn’t Wisconsin? appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Wisconsin septuagenarians conquer the American Birkebeiner
item.description: A grueling cross-country ski marathon in Wisconsin’s Northwoods, the American Berkebeiner on Feb. 21 attracts racers young and old. Racers age 70 and older find purpose and social bonds as they complete this extreme athletic feat year after year. The post Wisconsin septuagenarians conquer the American Birkebeiner appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Facing low wages and high prices, Wisconsin prisoners struggle to afford their cost of living
item.description: People incarcerated in Wisconsin’s jails and prisons have to pay for medicine, hygiene items, laundry, phone calls, entertainment and even health care. But with wages as low as 12 cents an hour, many go without — or go into debt. The post Facing low wages and high prices, Wisconsin prisoners struggle to afford their cost of living appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Support grows for Madison restaurant owner detained by ICE
item.description: Records show 50-year-old Noel Quintana was booked into an Indiana jail on an immigration hold at the end of January. The post Support grows for Madison restaurant owner detained by ICE appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Milwaukee’s 5 higher education leaders team up on AI
item.description: The leaders of Milwaukee’s five institutions of higher education are partnering with one of Wisconsin’s largest companies with the goal of making the region a nationally recognized leader for artificial intelligence and data science. The post Milwaukee’s 5 higher education leaders team up on AI appeared first on WPR.

item.title: A controversial herbicide is back. What does it mean for Wisconsin soybean growers?
item.description: Last week, the EPA reapproved dicamba for use on soybean and cotton crops after it was banned in 2024. The herbicide is the subject of thousands of complaints and lawsuits around the country, but Wisconsin has proven to be an outlier. The post A controversial herbicide is back. What does it mean for Wisconsin soybean growers? appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Milwaukee’s Listening Party looks for wisdom in the highs and lows on new album
item.description: Milwaukee’s Listening Party might be one of Wisconsin’s hardest working bands, playing around 120 gigs a year. The band aims for a new high with the release of its new record later this month. The post Milwaukee’s Listening Party looks for wisdom in the highs and lows on new album appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Wisconsin Assembly passes bill removing race-based higher ed programs
item.description: In moves they described as efforts to make the state's higher education system more meritocratic and safe for conservative students, Assembly Republicans voted Thursday to change eligibility for certain financial aid programs, and make it easier to sue universities for free speech violations.
